quest.title: Moulder of Mountains
quest.description: Following the instructions of Moon Carver, you arrive at Mt. Hulao in order to meet with Mountain Shaper.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Mora x12250, Adventurer's Experience x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: Have mercy, O mighty adeptus! I beg you... Show mercy upon me and my brother... Spare our lives!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: Who are you? What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We asked you first!

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: ...Oh! You enjoy safe passage in Jueyun Karst... It can only mean one thing!

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: You must be adepti messengers! Sent here to rescue me and my brother!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is he talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: ...Oh, have mercy, mighty messengers of the illuminated adepti! I beg you to save us... My brother and I, we only came here because our family is poor, and we heard tell of treasures hidden in the amber of Mt. Hulao.

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: It was stupid of us... but all we wanted to do was find enough treasure to sell and support our family...

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: We followed <color=#00E1FFFF>the path up the mountain</color>, but suddenly, the amber... it swallowed up my brother, Li Dang!

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: I ran away, and made it this far before it dawned on me: We were trespassers in the abode of the adepti, and this was our punishment...

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: I had no idea how to rescue my brother, so I just started praying for the adepti to have mercy, right here on the spot. And now, at long last, two messengers come to my aid...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? We're not adepti messengers... We just wanna find the adepti, like everyone else!

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: No no no, you must be messengers... You have to be!

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: I have no idea which amber trapped him... Please, you have to rescue him! I beg you, show me some adepti mercy!

choices.text: Oh, fine. I'll go have a look...

response.speaker: Li Ding
response.text: Thank you, thank you! O mighty messengers of the illuminated adepti, I promise that we will never be so foolish again...

choices.text: Of your transgression, your predicament, and your repentance, one has become aware.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, check you out! When you speak like that, you actually make a pretty convincing adepti messenger.

response.speaker: Li Ding
response.text: Thanks be to the adeptus of Mt. Hulao, and to their messengers! Never will we be so foolish again...

talks.objective: Shatter the amber on the mountain road to save the trapped person

dialogues.speaker: Li Dang
dialogues.text: *coughing*

dialogues.speaker: Li Dang
dialogues.text: Wh—What happened? ...Y—You rescued me? Thank you...

dialogues.speaker: Li Dang
dialogues.text: Oh! And have you seen my brother? His name is Li Ding, we were climbing the mountain together.

dialogues.speaker: Li Dang
dialogues.text: I just hope he didn't get trapped in amber too...

choices.text: He's the one who sent us looking for you.

response.speaker: Li Dang
response.text: Phew... so he's safe then...?

response.speaker: Li Dang
response.text: Thank you! I will head up to find my brother now.

response.speaker: Li Dang
response.text: Here's hoping I don't run into any more amber on the way...

choices.text: He's at the top of the mountain.

response.speaker: Li Dang
response.text: He made it to the top? That means he should be okay...

talks.objective: Talk to Li Ding and Li Dang

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: Thank you for rescuing my brother, O mighty messengers of the illuminated adepti.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have you ever seen the adeptus here?

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: What? No... I mean, like everyone else, we've heard that there's an adeptus living in Mt. Hulao.

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: But regular folks like us would never have the chance to meet them. No way.

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: Unlike you guys... You're adepti messengers, so it's a whole different story.

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: Anyway, we have trespassed in the realm of the adeptus for long enough. We should get going. Thank you, mighty adepti messengers...

dialogues.speaker: Li Dang
dialogues.text: Yes, thank you, messengers...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Boy, it'd be super helpful if we actually were adepti messengers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: 'Cause it seems like this adeptus has got a real temper problem...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But it's not like we've done anything wrong, so... hopefully we'll be okay... hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Mountain Shaper
dialogues.text: Who dares trespass on my mountain? Who is it that frees the thief from his incarceration?

dialogues.speaker: Mountain Shaper
dialogues.text: Foolish mortal, come forth and receive your punishment at once!

dialogues.speaker: Mountain Shaper
dialogues.text: ...You intrude upon the sanctity of Mt. Hulao, you destroy the amber of my mountain, and you free a thief whose freedom is not yours to give.

dialogues.speaker: Mountain Shaper
dialogues.text: The thieves' ignorance was an affront to the adepti... but your actions are an abomination of the highest order!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait! We can explain...

response.speaker: Mountain Shaper
response.text: ...A Sigil of Permission? One was unaware that such things still exist in the mortal realm.

response.speaker: Mountain Shaper
response.text: Is this... a Sigil of Permission? One is surprised to find that such things still exist in the mortal realm.

response.speaker: Mountain Shaper
response.text: In the beginning, Rex Lapis cast them for the mortals with his own hand. Few were made then, and thousands of years on, fewer still remain...

response.speaker: Mountain Shaper
response.text: Speak. One shall listen to the matter which brings you here, then one shall verify the truth thereof.

response.speaker: Mountain Shaper
response.text: You would be wise to speak the truth, for Liyue is not so far from here that one would be easily deceived.

response.speaker: Mountain Shaper
response.text: Rex Lapis... Assassinated?

response.speaker: Mountain Shaper
response.text: At the Rite of Descension!?

response.speaker: Mountain Shaper
response.text: What mortal in Liyue— nay, in all the world, would conspire to commit such foul treason? Or perhaps the more pertinent question is, what power in this world could aspire to achieve it?

response.speaker: Mountain Shaper
response.text: Rex Lapis charged the adepti with the protection of Liyue, and we have always honored this duty. As the people have prospered, so have we gradually withdrawn into the mountains. Indeed, this was a gesture of good will towards humanity.

response.speaker: Mountain Shaper
response.text: But now... Alas! Rex Lapis, gone...

response.speaker: Mountain Shaper
response.text: Traveler, of the matter you have relayed, one has become aware. One now knows why Moon Carver has sent for us.

response.speaker: Mountain Shaper
response.text: Once one has dealt with certain matters here that require my attention, one shall convene with the other adepti.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Can someone explain the amber situation to me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can! Adepti always have magical powers in storybooks, seems it's true in real life too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You know, like how grass is actually adepti hair, and rivers are actually adepti saliva... There must be something similar going on with the amber.

response.speaker: Mountain Shaper
response.text: ...Your nonsense knows no bounds. This amber is produced by a flower that one has planted here, called the karst crawler.

response.speaker: Mountain Shaper
response.text: The majority of the plant is hidden underground. When stepped on, it produces amber to trap the invader.

response.speaker: Mountain Shaper
response.text: After taking up residence here, one planted many karst crawlers to ensure that the tranquility of the mountain would remain undisturbed. Over the years, they have helped to prevent many disturbances, but in the process they have also trapped many curious things...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so the amber is... alive?

response.speaker: Mountain Shaper
response.text: Correct. Thus, one may not leave this place in its current state, for fear of the risk to innocent lives in one's absence.

response.speaker: Mountain Shaper
response.text: One will depart as soon as one has attended to this matter. One trusts that the manner of your departure will be swifter in nature.

choices.text: Amber must be crystallized adepti... ew, gross.

response.speaker: Mountain Shaper
response.text: Moon Carver... trusted a mere mortal as his messenger?

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: My brother told me everything... Thank you both so much for rescuing him!

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: *sigh* Our family has nothing to live on... We heard tell of treasures hidden in the amber of Mt. Hulao, and with nowhere else to turn, we came looking for them...

dialogues.speaker: Li Dang
dialogues.text: We weren't thinking straight... We thought that we could sneak up into the mountain and grab just enough treasure to sell and support our family with.

dialogues.speaker: Li Dang
dialogues.text: As you can see, the adeptus punished us for our greed. The amber swallowed me up, and if you hadn't come to my rescue, who knows when I would've gotten out.

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: Luckily, the adeptus was merciful. They sent you two as their messengers to save us...

response.speaker: Li Ding
response.text: Yes! You two saved my brother just as I was praying for the adeptus' forgiveness, right here on top of the mountain.

response.speaker: Li Dang
response.text: You are adepti messengers, no doubt about it.

response.speaker: Li Ding
response.text: We are truly blessed to receive the mercy of the adeptus. We promise that we will change our ways and make an honest living from now on. Even if it means sweating it out down at the docks.

response.speaker: Li Ding
response.text: Anyway, we have trespassed in the realm of the adeptus for long enough. We should get going. Thank you, mighty adepti messengers...

response.speaker: Li Dang
response.text: Yes, thank you, messengers...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Boy, it'd be super helpful if we actually were adepti messengers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: 'Cause it seems like this adeptus has got a real temper problem...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But it's not like we've done anything wrong, so... hopefully we'll be okay... hehe...

choices.text: Of your transgression, your predicament, and your repentance, one has become aware.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, your adepti messenger impression is really good. It's like this is the part you were born to play!

response.speaker: Li Ding
response.text: Thank you... yes, we are truly sorry, my brother and I have learned our lesson.

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: Please, help me rescue my brother. I don't know which amber it was that took him...

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: All I know is that we kept to <color=#00E1FFFF>the path the whole way up the mountain</color>. So the amber won't be far from the path.

dialogues.speaker: Li Ding
dialogues.text: O mighty messengers of the illuminated adepti, please rescue him, I beg of you...
